newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Two Taiwan navy frigates collide in training.
newsitem.headline: Two Taiwan navy frigates collide in training.

text.p: Two Knox-class frigates that Taiwan leased from the United States collided at sea during an operational exercise off a southern Taiwan naval base, military officials said on Friday.
No one was injured, but both frigates suffered unspecified damage, a navy spokesman told Reuters.
"The warships were practising operational tactics in the sea off our Tsoying base on Thursday," the spokesman said.
"One of the ships was supposed to turn, but somehow failed to do so. As a result, the prow of this ship hit the port of the other frigate.
"We have towed both ships back to the base and formed an ad-hoc committee to investigate the cause of the accident," the officer said.
The warships were among six Knox-class anti-submarine frigates that Taiwan leased from the United States in 1994 at a cost of some US$75 million per ship per year.
The deal drew bitter protests from communist China, Taiwan's rival since a civil war split the two in 1949.
Beijing, which views Taiwan as a rebel-held province, has warned other countries against arming the Nationalist-ruled island or recognising its exiled Republic of China government.
The frigates are equipped with high-tech anti-submarine weapons and submarine detection gear.
